title: Checkpoints with no category tests lower the evolution pass rate
reasoning: Replacing a zero test total with 1 turns a checkpoint with no tests in a category into a 0% pass-rate observation. The subsequent bin mean counts this as failure, lowering the displayed rate even though no tests failed. This also conflicts with the bar calculation, where zero-total, zero-passed rows do not affect an otherwise populated category's rate.
reproduction: Place two checkpoints from different problems in the same progress bin: one has 10 passed out of 10 category tests and the other has 0 out of 0. The evolution chart displays 50%, while the category bar displays 100%.
recommendation: Treat zero-total category rates as unavailable and exclude them from bin means. Preserve an unavailable state for bins with no evaluated tests.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were supplied, so coverage of categories absent from some checkpoints cannot be established.
suggestedRegressionTest: Cover progress bins containing evaluated suites, empty suites, and mixtures. Adding a checkpoint with no category tests must not change that category's measured pass rate.
minimumFixScope: Per-row rate calculation and bin aggregation in update_tests, with focused behavioral coverage.
